questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was in Italy. Both from a personal, cultural and academic perspective.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Lovely experience living in Milan. 
The communication from UniMi was a bit lacking and thus quite frustrating sometimes. 
Academic level and organisation (for some of the courses) was really bad.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was ok

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Slow to respond and lack of information of when they where ready to help.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Didn't line on campus

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
It's quite expensive. About the same as Copenhagen if you don't have a network. Ended up renting with a friend through AirBNB - about 6500 Dkk pr. persen a month.
Be aware of scammers - especially through Facebook pages

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Lots of scammers. 
You'll need a Fiscal Code (Tax code). The easiest way is to email the Danish Consulate - they have a template you can fill out.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Don't remember

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Don't remember

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Don't remember

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It's possible to change courses mid semester - be aware that some courses have attendance. You have to registre for the final exams.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take it easy

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not that many english options

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Lower level than KU. Many of the exams are multiple choice. Generally more "udenadslæring" than analytical thinking.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Depends on the teacher

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Behavioural Sociology
Society, Law, and Development
Smart Cities, Artificial Intelligence, and Digital Transformation Law
Global Criminal Organizations

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Behavioural Sociology - really interesting if you like experimental research designs 

DO NOT TAKE 'Global Criminal Organizations'
 - The professor (Francesco Landolfi) is the absolute worst. Unprofessional in every aspect (Often late, really bad english skills, incredibly boring lectures, no communication, extremely condescending, and so on) I CAN NOT STRESS THIS ENOUGH

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The public transportation system can easily be a lot of money. Get the student ATM card fast - it's only 22 euro a month and it's really worth it.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food it generally cheap - both in supermarkets and a restaurants. However i often ate at restaurants or went for aperitivo - it gets a bit expensive in the long run...

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Didn't participate in any clubs but there where quite a few. There is a Erasmus community which often arranged parties and trips to other italian cities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Travel Italy whenever you can. I bought a roadbike and it was a really nice way to see a lot of beautiful places and get some exercise

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Travel travel travel. Como is really nice and easy to get to. Try to avoid staying in the main city only. I also went to Lugano in Switzerland which is similar. 
Other cities that are quite close and that i would recommend are: Torino, Bergamo, Bologna,

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
It's quite easy and the Italians are generally sweet and don't mind speaking english even if they're not that good. 
Some things might take a bit more time - which can be a bit frustrating. But just take it easy and try not to stress too much about it.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: There are many small bars around the main campus where a lot of student are having aperitivo in the afternoon.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Ting tar tid

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: A lot. It's Italy after all.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. don't take a course where Francesco Landolfi is the professor (Global Criminal Organizations)
2. Get the student ATM card (public transportation) quick
3. You can take the exams multiple times even if you pass it the firs time. In this way you can also choose between several dates for each exam.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in Italy

Any other comments?

questions.answer: Yes
